PROBLEM OVERVIEW:

Task 1:Creating a function(summary statistics)

Summary statistics provide a numerical overview of a variables distribution:
Mean/average,standard deviation,median,minimum and maximum.

Define a function named 'calc_summary_stats' that takes a numeric vector 'x'

```{r}

calc_summary_stats <- function(x) {
  
x <- na.omit(x) # Remove any missing values (NA) to prevent calculation errors
  
# Calculate key summary statistics
  
  stats <- c(
    Mean   = mean(x),
    Median = median(x),
    SD     = sd(x),    # Standard Deviation
    Min    = min(x),
    Max    = max(x)
  )
  
  return(stats)  #Return the resulting vector of statistics
}

```
Task 2: using the dataset mtcars as example

Apply the function to the 'mpg' (Miles Per Gallon) variable from mtcars

```{r}
my_variable <- mtcars$mpg
summary_output <- calc_summary_stats(my_variable)

```
Print the output to the console
```{r}
print(summary_output)

```

Task 3: a function to calculate two sample t test and apply it

1. Define the core t-test function first,We name the function 'calc_two_sample_ttest', and it expects two inputs: group1 and group2

```{R}
calc_two_sample_ttest <- function(group1, group2) {
  test_result <- t.test(group1, group2) #Run R's built-in t-test function to compare the numbers in group1 and group2
  return(test_result)
}
```

 2. Define the wrapper function
This function automatically handles a whole dataset, picking out the columns you choose

```{r}
run_ttest_analysis <- function(data, value_col, group_col) {
  groups <- unique(data[[group_col]]) #Look at the grouping column and find all unique categories inside it (e.g., 4 and 6 cylinders)
  
  if(length(groups) < 2) {
    stop("The grouping column must contain at least two groups.") #Check if there are fewer than 2 groups; if so, stop the code and display an error message
  }

  #Extract all numbers belonging strictly to the first group
  g1_data <- data[[value_col]][data[[group_col]] == groups[1]]
  
  #Extract all numbers belonging strictly to the second group
  g2_data <- data[[value_col]][data[[group_col]] == groups[2]]
  
  #Send our two separated groups into our first function to run the t-test calculation
  
  result <- calc_two_sample_ttest(g1_data, g2_data)
  
  # Return the completed t-test output
  return(result)
}

```

 3. Filter your data
 Take the built-in 'mtcars' dataset and keep only the rows where the number of cylinders (cyl) is 4 or 6

```{r}
filtered_cars <- mtcars[mtcars$cyl %in% c(4, 6), ]
```
 4. Apply the wrapper function and explicitly PRINT the output where:
 
 Apply our wrapper function to the filtered data: 
 data = our filtered car dataset
 value_col = "mpg" (the numbers we want to compare)
 group_col = "cyl" (the groups we are comparing: 4 vs 6 cylinders)

```{r}
final_output <- run_ttest_analysis(data = filtered_cars, value_col = "mpg", group_col = "cyl")

#Print the final t-test results clearly
print(final_output)

```
